leaders.priorInstitution: Massachusetts Board of Regents for Higher Education (previously Chancellor of UMass Amherst 1971-79 and interim president of Westfield State College 1988-90)
leaders.nextRoleInstitution: Roxbury Community College (2002-2003, after several years away from a college presidency)
leaders.notes: Pioneering geologist and Tuskegee Airman; the only Black president in Springfield College's history and previously the first Black chancellor of UMass Amherst. Sources vary slightly on his exact end year (1997 vs 1998); died in 2013.
Brought out of retirement (he had led Slippery Rock University 1984-1997) to serve as interim president bridging the gap to Richard Flynn's arrival. Died in 2019.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean, College of Education (also Assistant to the Chancellor / Director, College of Information Science & Technology from 1995)
leaders.notes: 12th president; led the college for 14 years starting March 1999. Remained closely tied to the college after retiring, including a $1M gift in 2022.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Student Affairs
leaders.notes: 13th and current president, in office since August 2013; first woman to lead Springfield College.
Led the college (then College of St. Catherine) for 13 years before moving directly into the presidency of the Bush Foundation in 1997.

leaders.priorTitle: Held several academic leadership roles including interim president
leaders.notes: A Sister of the IHM order; served 18 years (joined August 1998). The exact coverage of the roughly one-year gap between Pampusch's 1997 departure and Lee's 1998 start (e.g., an unnamed acting president) is not documented in available sources -- inferred as a transition gap.
11th president and the university's first president drawn from business/nonprofit leadership rather than academia; announced retirement in 2024 after an eight-year tenure.

leaders.priorInstitution: Bloomfield College (until its 2023 merger with Montclair State University)
leaders.notes: 12th and current president, in office since July 2024; first African American president of St. Catherine University.

statusNote: Renamed from St. John Fisher College to St. John Fisher University in 2022; same continuously-led institution throughout.

leaders.notes: Fifth president and first woman to lead the college; died in office in September 2004 of complications from bone cancer. Doubled enrollment and added more than 20 academic programs during her tenure.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Dean of the College (previously VP for Administration, Dean of Faculty, and History Department chair)
leaders.notes: Sixth president. Named interim president immediately after Keough's death in September 2004, then formally appointed president in November 2005; capped a 40-year career at Fisher that began as a history professor in 1975.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice President for Enrollment, Advancement, and Planning
leaders.notes: Seventh and current president, in office since July 2015. Joined Fisher's administration in 1996 and rose through internal roles; oversaw the college's 2022 rebranding to St. John Fisher University.

15th president. Resigned in 2013 amid a financial-conflicts scandal involving a former dean and his own chief of staff; an independent investigation found errors in judgment and conflicts of interest but no criminal wrongdoing and no financial harm to the university.
16th president, serving as interim during the national search that followed Harrington's resignation (Aug 2013 - 2014). Passed away in 2024.

leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.notes: 17th president and the first layperson (i.e., not a Vincentian priest) to hold the role in the university's history, beginning July 2014. Retired in 2021 after a 36-year academic career; next role after retirement not documented.

18th and current president, began February 1, 2021. First non-Vincentian priest (member of the Dominican Order) to hold the presidency, ending the university's tradition of Vincentian-only presidents; previously the longest-serving president of Providence College (2005-2020).
